newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia invests in tourism to attract hard currency.
newsitem.headline: Croatia invests in tourism to attract hard currency.

text.p: Croatia will invest almost 300 million kuna ($50 million) in Adriatic resort hotels as part of a drive to bolster the country's main hard-currency earner for the coming tourist season, the government said on Friday.

"We had to help the Dalmatian economy, especially its tourist trade. (During the war, Dalmatian) hoteliers accommodated many refugees so the facilities are in bad shape," Finance Minister Bozo Prka told a news conference.
At a cabinet meeting on Thursday, the goverment approved a series of new measures, pledging guarantees for 140 million kuna in loans to 25 Dalmatian coast hoteliers, Prka said.
In a bid to make Croatia more competitive with other Mediterranean nations, the government this year gave up its tourist tax income.
The Croatian bank rehabilitation agency also agreed with Splitska Banka to reorganise 101.8 million kuna in matured loans which hoteliers are not able to repay now.
"We are also negotiating to get fresh loans totalling 350 million kuna from Austrian banks, with Croatian government guarantees," Prka said.
This would be on top of some 50 million German marks ($31 million) granted by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) for Zagreb's bid to spur private business.
He put the total to be invested in tourism through all these facilities at almost one billion kuna ($166 million).

Tourism was Croatia's main source of revenue while it was still a republic in federal Yugoslavia, ranking in between $4-5 billion a year. But the 1991-95 war with minority Serbs almost erased the country from the maps of world tour operators.
Tourism began to recover last year with a return of foreign travellers after an international peace accord was brokered in 1995, putting an end to the Balkan conflict.
"The Easter holidays have shown that our estimates of a 20 percent increase in tourisism trade for this year have been well-founded," Tourism Ministrer Niko Bulic said.
Tourism revenue from 1996 was put at $1.8-$2.0 billion.
